messages.author: d5b22c2be9055ac8
messages.subject: Re: ActiveX, internal error 429
parts:
Hi list,
I just received this strange error message after using the program without
a problem for months. Suddenly, I cannot open ANY existing projects,
including the sample projects. Nor can I creat new projects. I have
unistalled and reinstalled Distance 4.1, yet the problem persists. The
exact message I get when I attempt to open a file (File, Open, - then a
list of available files drops down - I click on one and this message
appears):

The following internal error has occurred in Distance.

AciveX component can't create object.
(Error raised from: Distance:ClsProject.ShowCommonDialog)
(Error source: D4Util)
(Error number: 429)

If you suspect that this error is caused by a bug in the program, please
note all of the above information and contact the program authors.

Press OK and Distance will try to recover from the error.
Press HELP for more information about internal errors in Distance.

[OK] [Help}


Any ideas?

Cheers,
Todd Plummer

messages.subject: Re: ActiveX, internal error 429
parts:
Dear Todd,
Being a programmer myself apart from being a wildlife researcher, I have met
similar problem in an application I designed some time ago. It to me seemed
like a bug that is caused by inappropriate positioning of commondialog.show
command in the source codes that is meant for the activeX object dialog box
used while opening a file. Another possibility, the system might have
possibly misplaced the required dll files.

But as you suggest that the software ran properly for few days and then
stopped functioning, would you check:

a. Whether any shared files (possibly .dll files) have been deleted
recently while uninstalling another application. The ocx file used for
common dialog box is also used by MS Office 2000. But again, I am not too
sure what may have caused the problem to persist despite reinstallation.

b. It is also possible that the support folder of distance files might
have got misplaced, moved or marked as 'read-only'.

I am sure Len must be writing something very soon with a proper solution,
just in case if any of these work.

Best regards,

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: ActiveX, internal error 429
parts:
Hi Todd,

(I'm cc'ing this to the list so it's in the archives for others)

Since you say that Distance worked fine for months, it must be that you are
encountering something Microsoft calls "DLL Hell" -- that is when some application
you have installed replaces a shared file (dll or other shared file) with either
(a) an older version of the same file (which install scripts should never do in
theory but sometimes do in practice), or (b) a newer version which has a bug in it
or breaks backward compatibility (again, should never happen in theory!). Quite
often, the problems are caused by Microsoft's own products!

Since the Open dialog shows on your screen, the source of the error is not likely
the common control dll. Also, the error message gives the error source as D4Util,
which is my utilities dll. I've had a look at my code ShowCommonDialog, and the
only D4Util routines that are called from there after you click "Open" is code to
extract the directory name from the file you chose to open. This code in turn uses
Microsoft Windows Script. So my guess is that your version of the Script engine
has been corrupted somehow. You don't say what version of Windows you're using but
I would guess it's Windows 2000 as that's the only version for which I can't bundle
scripting in with the Distance setup, for technical reasons. (I also can't bundle
it in with XP or Longhorn, but it shouldn't get corrupted on those systems.) In
any case, go to
http://www.microsoft.com/scripting
and download the appropriate version of Microsoft Windows Script 5.6 (or whatever
the latest version is) for your operating system and language. Install it, reboot,
and see if that fixes the problem.

In any case, please contact me off the list to say how you get on. If it works,
I'll add the fix to the list of known problems and solutions.

- Len


--
Len Thomas, Co-ordinator, Distance Development Project
Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
Centre for Research into Environmental and Ecological Modelling
The Observatory, University of St Andrews, Scotland KY16 9LZ
